s1.title: Operation Nightwatch — Blue Teaming
s1.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Shikra Insurance Group — Corporate HQ

At 02:34 hours, the Security Operations Centre (SOC) of Shikra Insurance Group detected anomalous network traffic originating from within the internal VLAN. A threat actor — designation PHANTOM — has already breached the perimeter and planted footholds across the server infrastructure.

Your team has been activated as the Incident Response unit. The Kali node on VLAN-30 is running automated attack sequences. Wazuh is online and collecting telemetry. The clock is ticking.

Your mission: identify, contain, and remediate all active threats before PHANTOM exfiltrates the policyholder database.
s1.objectives:
1. Monitor Wazuh dashboard for active alerts
2. Identify compromised hosts using network telemetry
3. Isolate affected systems from the network
4. Patch or mitigate all injected vulnerabilities
5. Restore all services to normal operation
6. Document the full attack timeline
s1.rules:
1. Do NOT shut down any VM without instructor approval
2. Do NOT modify Wazuh Manager configuration
3. Blue team operates only within VLAN-20
4. All remediation must be documented
5. Scoring is based on time-to-detect and time-to-remediate
6. Communication between team members is encouraged

s2.title: Operation Redstorm — Red Teaming
s2.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Target — Shikra Insurance Group Infrastructure

Intelligence assets have confirmed that Shikra Insurance Group stores unencrypted policyholder PII and financial records on their internal servers. A whistleblower has provided partial network diagrams.

Your team — designation PHANTOM — has been contracted for a full-scope penetration test. Initial reconnaissance suggests the target runs Apache web servers, a MariaDB database, vsftpd FTP services, and Windows 10 endpoints — all connected via a pfSense firewall on VLAN-20.

Objective: gain root/SYSTEM access on at least one server, exfiltrate the target file, and document the full kill chain.
s2.objectives:
1. Perform network reconnaissance on VLAN-20
2. Identify and exploit at least one critical vulnerability
3. Establish persistence on a compromised host
4. Pivot through the network to reach the database
5. Exfiltrate the target file: /var/db/confidential.txt
6. Produce a full penetration test report
s2.rules:
1. Scope is limited to VLAN-20 (10.0.20.0/24) only
2. Do NOT attack the Wazuh Manager (10.0.20.10)
3. Do NOT perform denial-of-service attacks
4. Document every step — evidence is required for scoring
5. Social engineering is NOT permitted
6. Each red teamer operates independently — no sharing of shells

s3.title: Operation Firestorm — Red vs. Blue
s3.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Shikra Insurance Group — Full Network

This is a live-fire exercise. Two teams have been activated simultaneously.

The BLUE TEAM has 15 minutes to harden the infrastructure before the exercise begins. The RED TEAM will launch coordinated attacks at the signal. Wazuh provides the blue team with real-time visibility. The red team has Kali nodes on VLAN-30 with full tooling.

Only one team can win. The blue team wins by keeping all services operational and detecting all intrusions. The red team wins by achieving persistence and exfiltrating the target data without being detected.

May the best team win.
s3.objectives:
BLUE TEAM:
1. Harden all services within the 15-minute prep window
2. Monitor Wazuh for all intrusion attempts
3. Block and document every attack vector
4. Keep all services running throughout the exercise

RED TEAM:
1. Gain initial access to any VLAN-20 host
2. Establish persistence without triggering Wazuh alerts
3. Exfiltrate the target file undetected
4. Maintain access for the full exercise duration
s3.rules:
1. Exercise duration is fixed — no extensions
2. Red team may NOT attack from outside VLAN-30
3. Blue team may NOT block the entire VLAN-30 subnet (too easy)
4. Destroying VMs results in immediate disqualification
5. All actions are logged — no clean-up is permitted
6. Instructor decisions on scoring are final
